newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-POCOCK LEADS NZ TO SOLID POSITION BY TEA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-POCOCK LEADS NZ TO SOLID POSITION BY TEA.

text.p: Opener Blair Pocock completed a maiden test half century on Friday as New Zealand moved to a strong first innings position in the first cricket test against England.
The home side had reached 154 for two at tea, with Pocock on 54 and Stephen Fleming unbeaten on 25, after England won the toss and invited them to bat.
England scored two breakthroughs in the post-lunch session, with Alan Mullally trapping Bryan Young leg before wicket for 44 and Dominic Cork having Adam Parore caught behind for six.
Pocock, in his test recall after being absent since the Lord's test of 1994 against England, reached his 50 from 160 balls in 229 minutes.
Fleming moved into his stride swiftly, steering left arm spinner Phil Tufnell to the third man fence to get off the mark, then effortlessly lofting him for six over long on.
In a generally mediocre English bowling effort, Cork had claimed one for 39 from 16 overs and Mullally one for 28 off 14.
